section_summary: This section follows Allied debate over the principles, adoption, review and public release of Japan’s proposed postwar constitution. It includes competing drafts, the Far Eastern Commission’s approved principles, directives to General MacArthur, his objection to publishing the directive, and disagreement over whether the Commission must approve the constitution before it takes effect. A Japanese Communist Party draft and a report on constitutional reform are also filed here.

subfiles.title: Appendix D: Proposed communication to General MacArthur
subfiles.about: Urges ample Diet debate, considers additional ratification methods, and defines the Far Eastern Commission’s role.
subfiles.summary: The draft argues that a rushed Diet vote would cast doubt on the Japanese people’s free consent and strain relations with other Allied governments. It proposes discussing a constituent assembly, a newly elected Diet or a referendum with Japanese leaders. It says the Far Eastern Commission should assess consistency with Allied requirements, preferably before the final Diet vote, without rewriting the constitution section by section.

subfiles.title: Annex to Appendix D: Article 73 of the present Constitution of Japan
subfiles.about: Reproduces the procedure for amending Japan’s existing constitution.
subfiles.summary: Article 73 requires an imperial proposal, a two-thirds quorum in each house and a two-thirds majority of those present.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Acheson on Dr. Evatt and constitutional adoption
subfiles.about: Assesses Evatt’s fear of hasty adoption and suggests a response based on existing directives.
subfiles.summary: Vincent considers a rushed Diet vote unlikely but says MacArthur has given no firm assurance of full debate. He suggests telling Evatt that Far Eastern Commission directives require adequate consideration, and describes a planned American policy statement on the Commission’s constitutional role.

subfiles.title: Note on basic principles for a new Japanese constitution
subfiles.about: Reports Acheson’s preference for Draft B or a broadly supported compromise.
subfiles.summary: Acheson preferred Draft B but favored a compromise that could gain majority support, including all four veto powers.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on competing Japanese constitution principles
subfiles.about: Compares four draft statements and asks whether the United States should continue supporting Draft B.
subfiles.summary: Vincent describes the origins and support for Drafts A through D. He favors the more detailed Draft B, which reflects earlier American thinking, while weighing a possible British veto against opposition to Draft D by the Soviet Union and others. He asks Acheson for guidance if compromise fails.

subfiles.title: Reform of the Japanese governmental system
subfiles.about: Sets proposed Allied objectives for representative government and safeguards concerning the Emperor.
subfiles.summary: The draft calls for representative institutions, civilian ministers, civil rights and effective legislative control of finances. It addresses alternatives for abolishing or retaining the Emperor institution and urges reforms that Japanese people will accept as lasting.

subfiles.title: Basic principles for a new Japanese constitution
subfiles.about: Proposes detailed democratic and constitutional requirements for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The draft specifies elected representative government, an independent judiciary, civil rights, elected local institutions and amendment by the people’s freely expressed will. It also proposes safeguards if the Emperor remains and rejects the existing powers of the Privy Council and House of Peers.

subfiles.title: Views of the United Kingdom on basic principles for a new Japanese constitution
subfiles.about: Proposes a shorter set of constitutional changes centered on responsible cabinet government.
subfiles.summary: The British paper favors amending the 1889 Constitution if reforms can gain durable Japanese acceptance.

subfiles.title: Reconciliation of United Kingdom views on constitutional principles
subfiles.about: States compromise principles including popular sovereignty, civilian cabinet government and civil rights.
subfiles.summary: The compromise calls for an elected Diet, independent judiciary, civil rights, elective local government and limited powers for the head of state.

subfiles.title: Transmission of approved constitutional principles
subfiles.about: Forwards the Far Eastern Commission’s approved principles for conversion into a directive.
subfiles.summary: Johnson reports unanimous approval on July 2 and asks that MacArthur be consulted about whether the policy should be released in Tokyo or Washington.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from minutes of the eighteenth Far Eastern Commission meeting
subfiles.about: Records unanimous approval of constitutional principles and a condition on press release.
subfiles.summary: Publication was deferred until MacArthur received the directive and chose whether release should occur in Tokyo or Washington.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding draft constitutional directive
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a draft directive reflecting the Commission’s July 2 decision.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring asks that the Joint Chiefs send the directive to MacArthur if it accurately states Commission policy.

subfiles.title: Draft directive on basic principles
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs MacArthur to ensure the adopted constitution conforms to the Commission’s principles.
subfiles.summary: The draft repeats requirements for popular sovereignty, representative institutions, civil rights, an independent judiciary and elected local government. It adds conditions concerning the Emperor, civilian cabinet ministers, the Privy Council and the House of Peers.

subfiles.title: Certification of Far Eastern Commission document
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached document as the Commission’s official July 2 text.
subfiles.summary: Johnson certifies unanimous adoption at the eighteenth meeting.

subfiles.title: Basic principles for a new Japanese constitution
subfiles.about: Sets the Commission’s approved standards for Japan’s new constitution.
subfiles.summary: The statement requires popular sovereignty, universal adult suffrage, civil rights, judicial independence and elective local government. It calls for reform or abolition of the Emperor institution, limits imperial powers if retained, and opposes retaining the Privy Council and House of Peers in their existing form.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on releasing the constitutional policy statement
subfiles.about: Requests MacArthur’s preference on the timing and location of press release.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring seeks transmission of the Commission’s question to MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Proposed communication to MacArthur about press release
subfiles.about: Asks MacArthur whether to release the policy in Tokyo or Washington.
subfiles.summary: It quotes the Commission’s unanimous decision to await MacArthur’s release preference.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum for ORI Report No. 3788
subfiles.about: Forwards a research report on Japanese progress toward constitutional reform.
subfiles.summary: The report assesses constitutional drafts and their implications for American policy.

subfiles.title: Comments on Japanese Progress Toward Constitutional Reform
subfiles.about: Evaluates the research study’s account of reform and possible postponement.
subfiles.summary: Kullgren summarizes conflicts between the old constitution and Allied aims, later Japanese reforms, and the Cabinet and party proposals. The memorandum judges the study valuable and says postponing ratification appears of doubtful benefit.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 495: Japan Communist Party draft constitution
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits the Communist Party’s Japanese draft and a newspaper account.
subfiles.summary: The mission encloses the documents but reports it cannot translate the draft because of a personnel shortage.

subfiles.title: Nippon Times: Draft Constitution Published by Reds
subfiles.about: Reports the chief provisions of the Japan Communist Party’s proposed constitution.
subfiles.summary: The party proposes a republic, abolition of the Emperor and peerage, equal rights, proportional elections and a single-house Diet.

subfiles.title: Enclosure identification for Japan Communist Party draft
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Identifies the Japanese-language draft as Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 495.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet for the party’s proposed constitution.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party proposed constitution
subfiles.about: Presents a proposed constitution for a Japanese people’s republic.
subfiles.summary: The draft’s preamble rejects the imperial system and calls for a people’s republic. Its articles address civil and political rights, labor and social rights, a unicameral national assembly, government, finance, courts, local administration and constitutional amendment. The Japanese text is heavily degraded in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: MacArthur message opposing public release of the directive
subfiles.about: Argues that publishing the constitutional directive would harm Japanese acceptance of reform.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur says the Cabinet draft conforms to the Commission’s principles. He warns that publication of a mandatory Allied directive would make voluntary Japanese reform appear imposed and asks for diplomatic discretion.

subfiles.title: Supplementary copy correcting MacArthur’s message
subfiles.about: Supplies a corrected ending for MacArthur’s release recommendation.
subfiles.summary: Corrects the wording requesting discretion in handling the directive.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding MacArthur’s views
subfiles.about: Forwards MacArthur’s response on public release of the policy.
subfiles.summary: Encloses MacArthur’s message opposing publication at that time.

subfiles.title: Copy of MacArthur’s response on public release
subfiles.about: Repeats MacArthur’s objection to publishing the Commission’s directive.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur says publication could make constitutional reform appear coerced.

subfiles.title: SWNCC memorandum returning release correspondence
subfiles.about: Explains that MacArthur had already replied through another cable channel.
subfiles.summary: Reid returns the proposed communication without Joint Chiefs action and attaches MacArthur’s reply and correction.

subfiles.title: Memorandum requesting consultation with MacArthur
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of the Commission’s request to consult MacArthur on a release date.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring forwards a proposed consultation under the Commission’s terms of reference.

subfiles.title: Proposed message seeking an acceptable release date
subfiles.about: Accepts temporary delay and asks when the policy may be published.
subfiles.summary: The Commission asks MacArthur to name a future press release date.

subfiles.title: McCoy letter on releasing constitutional principles
subfiles.about: Requests consultation with MacArthur about the eventual release date.
subfiles.summary: McCoy says the Commission accepts delay for now but wants the policy published at an early date.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Directive Serial No. 54
subfiles.about: Sends copies of the constitutional directive transmitted to MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: One copy is designated for the Commission and two for State Department files.

subfiles.title: Directive Serial No. 54: Basic principles for a new Japanese constitution
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Transmits the Far Eastern Commission’s approved constitutional principles as a directive.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur is instructed to ensure that any adopted constitution conforms to the Commission’s July 2 policy. The directive reproduces requirements for popular sovereignty, rights, representative institutions and safeguards concerning the Emperor and cabinet.

subfiles.title: McCoy letter on Commission authority to approve the constitution
subfiles.about: Seeks an American position after Soviet objections to a proposed review policy.
subfiles.summary: McCoy reports that ten Commission members favored a review proposal, while the Soviet delegate insisted that Commission approval was needed before the constitution could take effect. He encloses a suggested United States position and the Soviet statement.

subfiles.title: Soviet statement on Commission approval authority
subfiles.about: Argues that Commission approval is a prerequisite to the constitution taking effect.
subfiles.summary: The Soviet delegation rejects separating constitutional review from the question of legal effect. It interprets the Moscow decisions as requiring Commission agreement on the constitution’s acceptability, followed by a United States directive to MacArthur, before the new constitution may take effect.

subfiles.title: United States policy on Commission authority to approve a new constitution
subfiles.about: Defines Commission review as a check against Allied requirements rather than formal approval.
subfiles.summary: The draft says Japan may adopt a constitution under Japanese procedures if it meets the Potsdam Declaration and Commission policies. The Commission may examine the final draft and object to inconsistencies, but its terms of reference do not require affirmative approval before the constitution takes effect. Formal line-by-line approval is said to conflict with the Japanese people’s freely expressed will.

subfiles.title: Note forwarding provisions for constitutional review
subfiles.about: Forwards a Steering Committee proposal for later review of the constitution.
subfiles.summary: Notes Soviet reservation and New Zealand abstention on the enclosure.

subfiles.title: Provisions for the review of a new Japanese constitution
subfiles.about: Proposes Diet and Commission review one to two years after the constitution takes effect.
subfiles.summary: The proposal permits a referendum or other means of checking Japanese opinion.

subfiles.title: Reischauer memorandum on approval of the policy statement
subfiles.about: Reports internal approval of the attached American policy statement.
subfiles.summary: Penfield approved it for FE and Emmerson for JA.

subfiles.title: Filing Directive Serial No. 54 with the Commission
subfiles.about: Encloses a certified copy of the directive for Commission records.
subfiles.summary: Files Directive Serial No. 54 under the Commission’s terms of reference.

subfiles.title: Hilldring memorandum revising SWNCC 228/3
subfiles.about: Recommends replacing Appendix C and removing Appendix D references.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring proposes revisions to the United States constitutional adoption paper.

subfiles.title: Hilldring memorandum forwarding approved adoption policy
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Forwards SWNCC 228/8 as guidance for a Commission statement.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reports informal SWNCC approval of the policy on July 16.

subfiles.title: SWNCC approval of United States adoption policy
subfiles.about: Reports approval and distribution of policy on adopting a new Japanese constitution.
subfiles.summary: SWNCC approved the appendix of SWNCC 228/7 and requests distribution of SWNCC 228/8.
